question: An article published on 6 August 2023 in the Financial Times states that Ukraine joining the EU would weigh extremely heavily on the EU’s finances.

Based on an internal Council note they were able to consult, the authors of the article explain that the two biggest areas of the EU budget are the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and cohesion (regional spending), which together account for some 62% of the EU’s seven-year budget, or some 370 billion euros each1.

They draw attention to the fact that Ukraine, whose farmland exceeds the size of Italy and where the agricultural sector employs 14% of the population, would become the biggest recipient of CAP funding. The authors add that, according to another informal estimate, Ukraine’s entry into the EU would make France a net payer into the CAP.

Moreover, integrating this new Member State into the 2021-2027 cohesion budget would make it jump to the top of the list of recipients, dwarfing Poland’s 77 billion euro allocation. How does the Commission plan to overcome these potential obstacles?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) The Commission cannot comment on newspaper reports1 about internal documents of other institutions. As outlined in a Communication earlier in 20242, the impact of a future EU enlargement, including on the EU budget, will depend on: 1. the scope of enlargement, i.e. the number and relative size of the countries joining the EU; 2. the timing of enlargement, i.e.

the date of accession meaning when each of the countries joins; 3. the results of the accession negotiations - the enlargement is a merit-based process. Only when all the negotiations chapters (in particular the chapters on agriculture, cohesion and financial and budgetary provisions) are concluded, the budgetary impact on the EU budget will be known. 4. the EU acquis in force at the moment of the accession, i.e.

the policy design the EU chooses to apply will define the costs of enlargement; The reflections on the future of the EU budget – in terms of what it finances, how it finances it and how it is financed - are beginning. Such reflections are all encompassing.

Enlargement is one dimension under consideration together with the impact of global developments on the budget, Europe’s competitiveness on cutting edge technologies, climate transition and social fairness, just to name a few.
